limits: Verified never means interoperability with a device the design talks to unless a board measurement against that device is listed in the record; a design that checks its own output against its own model accepts its own symmetric mistakes.

Verified never means timing beyond the stated corner: a post-route timing result is for the part, speed grade, clock and tool version in its evidence file, not for other corners, temperatures or devices.

Verified never means beyond the widths and depths checked: a simulation covers the vectors it ran, a bounded formal result covers the stated depth only, and a per-width proof covers the widths it names; only a Lean proof marked all widths covers every width, and only for its model.

Verified never means the requirement is the right one: the text of a requirement is the human's check (or the planner's, where the record says delegated), and a record shows that checks exist and pass, not that nothing was left out.
Verified never means a hardware or board result unless a board measurement item is listed; a simulation is not the board.
Verified is about the files in the manifest at the hashes given. A change to any of them makes the record out of date (the CI check fails), and the evidence stale until it is re-recorded.
An agreement or acceptance recorded as delegated is the planner's decision on the owner's delegation, not a human sign-off; the record counts it apart.
1 formal items are bounded model checks; each holds to its stated depth only: V-DIV-FORMAL-FAULTS.
1 performance requirements are verified by post-route timing at one corner: DIV-P-OOC.
name: divider
notes: Arithmetic library function divider (brief 139b). Every requirement is a draft written by the agent from the owner's request (spec_status: draft; only a human sets agreed). Evidence is generated by `python -m pytest arith/divider/tests --junitxml=results/139b_arith/divider_junit.xml` with ARITH_RECORD_DIR=results/139b_arith. The Lean items show 'statement not approved': lean_approvals.yaml is the owner's. The one performance requirement (brief 160) says every prepared out-of-context point has a routed Vivado result; no Fmax or area bound is agreed.

item_views.title: The formal reference and fault-catching tests pass
Reference proofs: jobs proved unbounded, none failed
Six seeded faults each make the proof fail (bounded model checking)

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end: each variant equals an independent reference (SystemVerilog `/` and `%`, the divide-by-zero convention) for all input sequences from reset: 14 jobs at W = 4, 5 and 6, iterative and pipelined, PIPE = 1 to 4; unbounded (abc pdr). Six seeded faults are applied to the RTL and the same proof fails (bounded model checking finds the counterexample), which shows the harness is not vacuous.
requirements.title: Every variant equals an independent reference (SymbiYosys)

item_views.title: Variant pairs proved equal, none failed

requirements.title: Variants of the function agree with each other (SymbiYosys)

item_views.title: Restoring division equals Nat.div and Nat.mod, every width
Restoring division by zero returns all ones and the dividend, every width

requirements.text: The restoring recurrence of div_restoring_*.sv computes n / d and n % d for every width, and for d = 0 returns all ones and n. Proved for all widths in Lean, statement not approved; the Lean text is a transcription of the RTL's step, cross-checked against the Python model for W <= 5; register widths are not modelled.
requirements.title: Restoring division is correct for every width (Lean)

item_views.title: Non-restoring division with its final correction equals Nat.div and Nat.mod, every width

requirements.text: The non-restoring recurrence of div_nonrestoring_*.sv, with its final correction, computes n / d and n % d for every width and d > 0 (invariant: a non-negative partial remainder is n - d*Q, a negative one n - d*(Q+1), always in [-d, d)). Proved in Lean, statement not approved; division by zero is not part of this theorem (covered by simulation and the formal reference).
requirements.title: Non-restoring division with correction is correct for every width (Lean)

requirements.text: Each point of the build files of divider (build/<variant>/build.yaml; 28 in all, both parts) goes through Vivado 2026.1 out-of-context synthesis, placement and routing and leaves a recorded result (utilisation, WNS, WHS, Fmax, logic levels, vectorless power) in verif/results/vivado_ooc_<variant>_<part>.json. The measured values and each point's pre-stated expectation are in the Measured table of spec.md and in verif/results/vivado_surface.json; this requirement states only that the measurement exists for every point, because no Fmax or area bound has been agreed.
